module

public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Diam
public import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic
public import FormalConjecturesForMathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.VertexDistance

@[expose] public section

namespace SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/-- The set of vertices of maximum eccentricity. -/
noncomputable def maxEccentricityVertices (G : SimpleGraph α) : Set α :=
  {v : α | G.eccent v = G.ediam}

/-- The average eccentricity of a graph `G`: the mean of `G.eccent v` over all vertices,
converted to a real number. Returns 0 if the graph has no vertices. -/
noncomputable def averageEccentricity (G : SimpleGraph α) : ℝ :=
  (∑ v : α, (G.eccent v).toNat) / (Fintype.card α : ℝ)

/-- The diameter of a finite graph as a computable natural number: the maximum BFS distance
(`computable_dist`) over all ordered pairs of vertices. -/
def computable_ediam (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℕ :=
  Finset.univ.sup fun p : α × α => computable_dist G p.1 p.2

/-- For a connected finite graph, the extended diameter `ediam` equals the computable diameter. -/
theorem ediam_eq_computable (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty α]
    (hc : G.Connected) : G.ediam = (computable_ediam G : ℕ∞) := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · rw [ediam_le_iff]; intro u v
    rw [← (hc.preconnected u v).coe_dist_eq_edist, dist_eq_computable]
    exact_mod_cast Finset.le_sup (f := fun p : α × α => computable_dist G p.1 p.2) (Finset.mem_univ (u, v))
  · obtain ⟨p, -, hp⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_sup (Finset.univ : Finset (α × α)) Finset.univ_nonempty
      (fun p : α × α => computable_dist G p.1 p.2)
    have hp' : computable_ediam G = computable_dist G p.1 p.2 := hp
    rw [hp', ← dist_eq_computable, (hc.preconnected p.1 p.2).coe_dist_eq_edist]
    exact edist_le_ediam

/-- The eccentricity of a vertex `u` in a finite graph as a computable natural number:
the maximum BFS distance (`computable_dist`) from `u` to any vertex. -/
def computable_eccent (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (u : α) : ℕ :=
  Finset.univ.sup fun v => computable_dist G u v

/-- The radius of a finite graph as a computable natural number: the minimum, over all vertices,
of the computable eccentricity. -/
def computable_radius (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty α] : ℕ :=
  Finset.univ.inf' Finset.univ_nonempty (computable_eccent G)

/-- For a connected finite graph, the eccentricity `eccent u` equals the computable eccentricity. -/
theorem eccent_eq_computable (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty α]
    (hc : G.Connected) (u : α) : G.eccent u = (computable_eccent G u : ℕ∞) := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · rw [eccent_le_iff]; intro v
    rw [← (hc.preconnected u v).coe_dist_eq_edist, dist_eq_computable]
    exact_mod_cast Finset.le_sup (f := fun v => computable_dist G u v) (Finset.mem_univ v)
  · obtain ⟨v, -, hv⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_sup (Finset.univ : Finset α) Finset.univ_nonempty
      (fun v => computable_dist G u v)
    have hv' : computable_eccent G u = computable_dist G u v := hv
    rw [hv', ← dist_eq_computable, (hc.preconnected u v).coe_dist_eq_edist]
    exact edist_le_eccent

/-- For a connected finite graph, the radius `radius` equals the computable radius. -/
theorem radius_eq_computable (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty α]
    (hc : G.Connected) : G.radius = (computable_radius G : ℕ∞) := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · obtain ⟨u0, -, hu0⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_inf' (Finset.univ_nonempty) (computable_eccent G)
    have h0 : computable_radius G = computable_eccent G u0 := hu0
    rw [h0, ← eccent_eq_computable G hc u0]
    exact radius_le_eccent
  · obtain ⟨u1, hu1⟩ := G.exists_eccent_eq_radius
    rw [← hu1, eccent_eq_computable G hc u1]
    exact_mod_cast Finset.inf'_le (computable_eccent G) (Finset.mem_univ u1)

end SimpleGraph

findings.description: On disconnected graphs, this computes the maximum diameter of a connected component, not Mathlib's diameter or its natural-valued conversion. For the graph on Fin 3 with the sole edge {0,1}, Lean verifies computable_ediam = 1, whereas ediam = ⊤ and diam = 0. The documented maximum-BFS-distance formula accurately describes this convention, and ediam_eq_computable correctly requires connectedness; nevertheless, the mathematical difference from the neighbouring Mathlib API merits explicit treatment. Current problem uses supply connectedness and are unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Diam.lean defines ediam using extended distances and diam := ediam.toNat; diam_eq_zero_of_not_connected gives zero for disconnected graphs. https://mathworld.wolfram.com/GraphDiameter.html states: “A disconnected graph has infinite diameter.” VertexDistance.lean documents that computable_dist returns zero for unreachable vertices.
findings.suggested_fix: For a Mathlib-compatible natural-valued diameter, guard the current maximum with `if G.Connected then ... else 0`. This agreement with G.diam was proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean. Alternatively, retain the componentwise invariant but explicitly distinguish its disconnected-graph semantics from ediam and diam.

findings.description: Because unreachable BFS distances contribute zero, this is the eccentricity of u within its connected component. It is not generally `(G.eccent u).toNat`. On the graph with edge {0,1} and isolated vertex 2, Lean verifies computable_eccent G 0 = 1, while G.eccent 0 = ⊤ and its toNat conversion is 0. This is a defensible computational convention, explicitly specified through computable_dist, but differs mathematically from the Mathlib notion suggested by the API. The connectedness hypothesis in eccent_eq_computable prevents incorrect current uses.
findings.source_evidence: Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Diam.lean proves eccent_eq_top_of_not_connected for every vertex; ENat.toNat_top = 0. https://mathworld.wolfram.com/GraphEccentricity.html assigns infinite eccentricity to every vertex of a disconnected graph, while explicitly noting that Wolfram Language's VertexEccentricity instead uses the containing component. Thus the componentwise convention exists, but is distinct from Mathlib's convention.
findings.suggested_fix: To agree with the natural conversion of Mathlib eccentricity, use `if G.Connected then` the current maximum `else 0`; the resulting equality with `(G.eccent u).toNat` was proved in the scratch file. Alternatively, explicitly expose this as component eccentricity and document the distinction.

findings.description: On a disconnected nonempty graph, this returns the minimum radius among its connected components, rather than Mathlib's radius or its natural conversion. For two disjoint edges on Fin 4, Lean verifies computable_radius = 1, whereas radius = ⊤ and radius.toNat = 0. The formula is consistent with the file's documented computable eccentricity, so this is a non-standard convention concern rather than an incorrect proved lemma. All existing uses employ radius_eq_computable with connectedness.
findings.source_evidence: Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Diam.lean defines radius as the infimum of extended eccentricities and proves radius_eq_top_of_not_connected. https://mathworld.wolfram.com/GraphRadius.html states that radius is the minimum vertex eccentricity and that a disconnected graph therefore has infinite radius.
findings.suggested_fix: For compatibility with G.radius.toNat, return zero when G is disconnected, or take the minimum of a Mathlib-compatible corrected computable_eccent. The guarded version's agreement with G.radius.toNat was proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean. Otherwise, explicitly document the minimum-component-radius convention.

reformulations.difference: The source defines B as the vertices of maximum eccentricity; Lean uses equality of eccentricity with ediam.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Mathlib defines ediam = ⨆ w, G.eccent w. Consequently, G.eccent v = G.ediam iff every G.eccent w ≤ G.eccent v. This equivalence was proved without finiteness assumptions. WOWII definition 55 explicitly identifies B with the periphery, noting that the site previously called it the boundary; thus the use sites do not mistakenly substitute periphery for a different boundary notion.

reformulations.difference: Lean sums natural-number conversions of the extended eccentricities, casts the sum to ℝ, and then divides, rather than writing the real arithmetic mean directly.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On the source's finite connected graphs, every eccentricity is finite, so conversion preserves every summand; the division occurs in ℝ, not ℕ. More generally, I proved that this definition equals `((∑ v, (G.eccent v : ℝ≥0∞)) / Fintype.card α).toReal` for every finite graph. In the disconnected case every eccentricity is ⊤, and both real-conversion expressions are zero; the empty case is also zero. Both conjecture use sites assume connectedness.

reformulations.difference: WOWII definition 52 maximizes distance to B over vertices outside B, while the Lean statement uses eccSet, whose outer maximum includes all vertices.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Vertices already in B have distance zero to B, so adding them cannot change a nonnegative maximum. The peripheral set is nonempty for a nonempty finite graph. With the zero convention for an empty outer maximum, the equality `G.eccSet S = G.ecc S` holds for every finite graph and set S; this identity and the corresponding inequality equivalence were proved in Lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses eccSet and multiplies the source's inequality by the positive minimum local independence number of the complement, avoiding division.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The source HTML genuinely puts an overline on G, and definition 4 specifies local independence. The explicit positive-denominator hypothesis ensures that `2*p ≤ t*q` is equivalent to `(2*p : ℝ)/q ≤ t`. This equivalence, combined with eccSet = ecc for the source's outside-the-set maximum, was proved in Lean. The restriction excludes precisely the undefined zero-denominator case.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses eccSet, clears the radius-of-the-square denominator, and explicitly assumes that denominator is positive.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The set-eccentricity expressions coincide as above. Positive-denominator cross-multiplication was proved in Lean. I also proved that the square of a connected nontrivial finite graph has positive finite radius: it contains every edge of G and remains connected. Thus the added positivity hypothesis follows from the other hypotheses.

review.notes: Checked all five definitions and all three proved lemmas, including their actual typeclass parameters and every use site found by declaration-name searches. No incorrect proved lemma or inherited conjecture misformalization was found. The three findings are deliberately classified as questionable: their componentwise BFS semantics are documented, but differ from Mathlib on admissible disconnected inputs. All current conjecture and computational-test uses satisfy connectedness. Boundary examples and proposed Mathlib-compatible guards compile in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/equivalence.lean; tests cover empty and singleton graphs, complete graphs, a three-vertex path, an edge plus an isolate, and two disjoint edges. The three compatibility lemmas have no sorryAx dependency. The target source was not modified. The live WOWII server was unreachable; statements, definition popups and status remarks were read from July 2026 archived captures. No claim is made about subsequent live-site status updates.
